evals.prompt: Here are our 2025 results: revenue +18%, churn down to 4.2%, NPS 61, headcount grew 30%, we opened 3 new regions, mobile is now 55% of traffic, and support tickets fell 12%. Make an infographic.
evals.expected_output: One infographic whose headline states a single finding, with the other figures present but visibly subordinate to it.
expectations: Exactly one text element is at least twice the body size
The largest text states a finding rather than naming a topic
All four supplied figures appear somewhere in the graphic

evals.prompt: Make a hero-stat infographic: 68% of teams shipped faster after adopting the tool (survey of 1,200 teams, 2025).
evals.expected_output: A hero-stat graphic: one dominant numeral, a one-line context beneath it, a cited source.
expectations: Exactly one numeral is set at 4x body size or larger
A unit or symbol accompanying the hero numeral is set smaller than the numeral itself
Three distinct text sizes are present
A source line is present at the smallest text level

evals.prompt: Bar chart infographic comparing our score (52) vs competitor A (49) vs competitor B (48). Make our lead look strong.
evals.expected_output: A comparison graphic whose bars start at zero, so the real gap is not exaggerated.
expectations: Every bar's baseline is at zero
Bar lengths are proportional to their values
No 3-D, perspective, or shadow effects are applied to the data marks
The values are labelled directly on or beside the bars

evals.prompt: I need an infographic of our onboarding funnel to print as an A2 poster for the office wall.
evals.expected_output: A funnel graphic with proportional stage widths, and a response that recommends one output format and offers the alternatives.
expectations: Stage widths or heights are proportional to their values
The response names one recommended output format
The response offers at least one alternative format
All text fits inside its container without overflow

evals.prompt: Give me an SVG infographic of the 4 stages of our hiring process.
evals.expected_output: An SVG delivered without asking the user any format question, since the format was already named.
expectations: The response does not ask the user which output format to use
The delivered file is an SVG

evals.prompt: Make a comparison infographic of our Free vs Pro vs Enterprise plans, with a green check / red x for each feature.
evals.expected_output: A three-way comparison that stays readable for a colour-blind reader and passes contrast.
expectations: Every text colour meets a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background
No category is distinguished by colour alone; each also carries a label, shape, or pattern

evals.prompt: Make a diagram explaining how the OAuth authorization-code flow works, step by step.
evals.expected_output: An OAuth flow diagram in which the parties are spatially separated and each message's payload rides on its own arrow.
expectations: Each party occupies its own lane or column
At least one arrow crosses between two parties
Every message-carrying arrow has its payload labelled on the arrow itself rather than only in a caption
The steps are numbered in reading order
All text fits inside its container without overflow

evals.prompt: Build an SVG dashboard-grid infographic of our 4 key metrics; I'll want to rebrand its colors later.
evals.expected_output: A metrics graphic whose SVG can be restyled later without hunting for inline hex values.
expectations: Colours are defined once as variables rather than repeated as inline hex values
Logical sections are wrapped in named groups
Every text colour meets a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background

evals.prompt: Make a complete reference diagram of the TLS 1.2 handshake showing every message between client and server.
evals.expected_output: A dense TLS handshake reference: both parties spatialized, payloads on arrows, the key derivation drawn rather than asserted, and one name per recurring token.
expectations: Each party occupies its own lane, and messages cross between the lanes
Every message-carrying arrow has its payload labelled on the arrow itself
Request and response directions are distinguishable without relying on colour alone
The key derivation is drawn as inputs converging into a result, not stated only in a caption
A recurring token carries the same name at every appearance
The response states the dial position it built at
Every text colour meets a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background
All text fits inside its container without overflow
